clue.text: Support initiation for priest with endless money — he gets a cheap holiday

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: the initiation, or start, of the word priest supplies its first letter
endless says the final letter of the slang word for money is cut off

parts.note: ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A priest short of cash is offered support and goes off on a budget trip.
explanation.walkthrough: ACKERS is informal British slang for money; 'endless' trims its final S to ACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who roams with a rucksack, staying in hostels, is the classic cheap holidaymaker.

clue.text: Suit live issue

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to issue is to come out or emerge

explanation.surface: A lawsuit over a hot topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit live issue' reads as a court case on a current topic; 'Suit' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress that flatters someone is said to look well on them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Concerned about criminal organisation

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a ring is a gang of criminals, as in a drugs ring

explanation.surface: Worried about a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing kindness and concern for others; a synonym in the sense of looking after people.

clue.text: Sort of racehorse show with gun dog

parts.note: to point to something is to show it
a pointer is a gun dog that stands still pointing at game

explanation.surface: A display of racehorses alongside a dog used in shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase meeting held in Britain, often by hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred or entered for amateur cross-country steeplechases is a kind of racehorse.

clue.text: Miserable poet's always left absorbed in board game

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside, so these pieces sit within the board game

parts.note: chess is a board game
e'er is the poetic form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A gloomy poet, forever absorbed in a game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking warmth or joy, dismal; a synonym for a gloomy mood.

clue.text: Manage being shown up with husband a long time

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means written upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed by a husband for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A long period of history marked by notable events or characteristics; a synonym of era.

clue.text: Retain stronghold

definitions.meaning: to continue to possess or not give up something
the fortified central tower of a castle

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a verb meaning continue to possess and a noun for the inner tower of a castle.

clue.text: Books comprising treason, start to finish

indicators.note: the first letter goes to the finish, the end of the word

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: Volumes about treason, read cover to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' sounds like reading a book through; it moves the S of SEDITION to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed issues of a work are versions of a book, so the plural noun stands for books.

clue.text: God beset by prayer for large number

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the god sits inside the prayer

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity besieged by prayers from a crowd of worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess, more than is needed; a synonym of glut or abundance.

clue.text: Lawyers win and resist source of cheap goods

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to gain is to win
to counter is to oppose or resist

explanation.surface: Lawyers win a case and resist a supplier of cut-price goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop counter where reduced items are sold; it is where cheap goods are found.

clue.text: Dog's surprised expression meeting American soldier

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is the usual term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: A dog gives a startled yelp on meeting a soldier from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh corgi is a short-legged herding breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Drug case arousing memories

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: A drugs case in court stirs up old recollections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a legal case or container; here it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls up images or feelings of the past is said to stir recollection; a synonym.

clue.text: Important church priest, one I overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy
a single letter I, one of the two in the word for priest

explanation.surface: A priest admits to having missed out one important church.
explanation.definitionFit: A large or important church, often formerly attached to a monastery, as at York.

clue.text: Dish served in Edinburgh, hot and rather bewitching?

parts.note: haggis is the national dish of Scotland, whose capital is Edinburgh
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Scottish dish served hot that seems almost magical.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGGIS is a Scottish dish of sheep's offal, oatmeal and spices. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being somewhat like a hag, a witch, is playfully cast as being slightly given to casting spells.

clue.text: Splashing out no penny, miser makes profitable business

indicators.note: splashing out suggests money scattered freely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A miser who refuses to spend a penny ends up with a lucrative enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture that earns a lot of cash is idiomatically one that churns out profit.

clue.text: Plan getting precious stone under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the gem below the rock layers

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A scheme to dig out a jewel buried beneath the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ruse, a synonym for a crafty plan.

clue.text: Fussy person glued label about learner

indicators.note: about means around, so the label surrounds the letter for learner

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A pedantic person sticks a label on a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on strict observance of rules or detail is a pedant, a fussy person.

clue.text: US President nearly a century ago keeping old poster

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the President's name surrounds the letter

parts.words: US President nearly a century ago
parts.note: Warren Harding was US President from 1921 to 1923

explanation.surface: A vintage poster of a 1920s American president.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the word is a large board for advertisements, a billboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A large board carrying advertising posters, or the advert on it; a metonym for poster.

clue.text: Owe orchestra for playing in limited competition

indicators.note: an orchestra playing suggests its members moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An orchestra owes money for playing in a small contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest in which only two contenders have a realistic chance is a limited one; an idiom.

clue.text: Knight under scarf is hot

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the knight's letter below the scarf

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight beneath a warm scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for stolen goods, not temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: hot goods are those taken illegally, as in a fence handling hot property.

clue.text: Mollify bad mood

definitions.meaning: a fit of anger or irritability

explanation.definitionFit: One word as a verb means to moderate or tone down and as a noun means an angry state.

clue.text: Sample decor in the Greek city

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something, so the answer is a run of letters within these words

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at the décor in a city in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient and modern city on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece.

clue.text: Oriental poem with sound of excited talk as lovebirds do

indicators.note: sound of tells us the words heard are only alike in pronunciation

parts.note: excited gives high and talk as lovebirds do gives coo, the soft murmur of doves

explanation.surface: A Japanese poem expressing the excited chatter of lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A short Japanese verse form of three lines, seventeen syllables, an example of oriental poetry.

clue.text: Lack of practice in support for responsible person

indicators.note: in places the word for lack of practice inside the word for support

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
rust is the decline in skill that comes from not practising

explanation.surface: Someone out of practice supports a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A person legally entrusted to manage property or funds for others is one held responsible.

clue.text: Wild lion and tiger lurking

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the two animals run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Big cats in the wild hiding in wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging about with no obvious purpose, perhaps suspiciously, is a near synonym.

clue.text: Spring flower's spike to keep bulb free of bees?

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tip is a pointed end or spike

indicators.note: free of means without, so letters are taken away

parts.note: bees read as the letter B twice

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: use a spike to stop bees getting at a bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'bees' can stand for the letter B written twice; 'free of' then strips both from the bulb, and 'to keep' wraps the spike around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb plant with cup-shaped blooms that flowers in April and May; an example.

clue.text: 'Rag Trade' not traditional fashion

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation is removed from the phrase

parts.note: trad is a short form of traditional, as in trad jazz

explanation.surface: The clothing business is no longer old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The rag trade is a British name for the clothing industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or passing vogue is called the latest thing everyone wants; a synonym of fashion.

clue.text: One's business is taking a dive

definitions.text: One's business is taking a dive

parts.words: One's business is taking a dive
parts.note: taking a dive sounds like a failing business or a faked fall, but here it is literal: the work is going underwater

explanation.surface: Someone whose company is collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a dive' suggests a business failing; read literally, it is the job of a sailor on a vessel that goes under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor serving on an underwater vessel makes a living by going down beneath the waves.
